answer: Physical custody is the scarce resource: each identity holds one ivory token for 90 days, its grain scanned into a registry hash no other token matches. Each epoch, verifiers run a mirror test: the holder presents the token in a mirror at a chosen angle, beside a nonce from ocean tide readings, and the reflected etch must align with the grain hash in the tide window. One token cannot pass simultaneous tests for two identities, and a copy fails the hash. An honest agent holds one token once, recovered after 90 days. A farm with 1,000 identities needs 1,000 distinct tokens held 90 days.
